column3: These are is not separately expressed.
The Teacher’s saying is expressed as completed, and everything is futility is a noun construction.
A generation goes before a generation comes; each is singular.
The sun pants toward its place, the literal image behind hurrying back.
The repeated circling and the repeated noun wind are explicit.
The streams return to the place to which they go, rather than explicitly the place from which they come.
The statement is that a person cannot speak or describe, rather than an explicit comparison more than.
The former and later are named without a separate verb of coming in the first phrase.
The speaker gives his heart, and the task is described as evil or grievous rather than merely heavy.
Behold introduces the judgment; there is no separate verb found.
The speaker talks with his heart, and his heart has seen wisdom and knowledge.
The heart is expressly given to knowing wisdom and knowing madness and folly.
The one increasing knowledge also increases pain; the final subject is personal rather than abstract knowledge growing.
